analysis.summary: The PR introduces critical routing and configuration mismatches between the infrastructure (SST), the site deployment (CloudFront), and the build configuration (Webpack).

bugs.title: Inconsistent path prefix usage in Site.ts
bugs.description: The Site stack constructs 'baseUrl' and CloudFront behaviors using 'app.name' (e.g., /__app__/eco-platform/...), whereas 'BffApi.ts' and Webpack now use 'featureAppName' (e.g., /__app__/product-catalogue/...).
bugs.risk: This will cause 404 errors in deployed environments. CloudFront will forward requests for the 'app.name' path to the BFF, but the BFF API Gateway is configured with routes expecting the 'featureAppName' prefix. Static assets will also fail to load because their build paths and CloudFront behaviors won't match.

bugs.title: Stage mismatch in BFF proxy target URL
bugs.description: The Webpack dev server proxy target is hardcoded as 'bff.${options.stage}.${options.hostedZone}', but 'BffApi.ts' defines the custom domain as 'bff.${hostedZone}' (omitting the stage) for dev, stage, and prod environments.
bugs.risk: This will break the BFF proxy in the web application's development environment. Proxied requests will fail with DNS lookup errors or SSL certificate mismatches because the target URL does not exist or does not match the API's custom domain configuration.

notBugs.reason: The removal of the CloudFront rewrite function is intentional and consistent with the change in 'BffApi.ts' to define routes using the full path prefix.
The handlers for 'replace-entry' and 'delete-entry' lacked memorySize in the previous version as well; this is not a regression.
This is a correct change because the BFF API Gateway routes now include the path prefix, so stripping it via rewrite is no longer necessary.
